newsitem.title: UK: Brit Energy buys 12.5 pct in Humber Power.
newsitem.headline: Brit Energy buys 12.5 pct in Humber Power.

text.p: British Energy said on Monday that it had acquired a 12.5 percent interest in Humber Power Ltd for a consideration of up to 28 million stg.
Humber Power is the owner and operator of the 1,260 megawatt combined cycle gas-fired plant at Stallingborough in northern England.

The consideration comprises payments up to a maximum of 20 million stg for the equity and a commitment to subscribe for eight million stg of short term loan stock, repayable in 2001. "This investment is in line with British Energy's strategy to diversify its plant and fuel mix by investing in non-nuclear generation assets in the UK," the company said.
Elf Exploration UK, a subsidiary of Elf Aquaitane has also purchased a 12.5 percent interest in Humber Power on the same terms.
Apart from Elf, British Energy's other partners in the project are Imatran Voima Oy, Midlands Electricity, Tomen Power Corporation and ABB Energy Ventures.
The first phase (750 MW) of the South Humber project is due to be commissioned soon while the second phase (510 MW) would be on stream in 1999.
